note: Stable reusable panel. Same roster shops any future redesign of this site. Intent mix per gauntlet spec, translated for a course/coaching store (decisions.md D7). 12 mobile / 8 desktop. Cards contain zero site-positioning language (firewall).

buyers.name: Maritza Okafor
buyers.backstory: ER nurse coming off a run of night shifts; a coworker showed her a 'nerve-calming drawing' video on TikTok.
buyers.errand: Buy a beginner-friendly calming drawing course tonight for under $70. You half-remember the word 'neurographica'.
bail_triggers: checkout asks for more than card+email basics
can't find the price after 3 screens
buyers.trust_needs: a clear price before checkout and some sign real people took the course
habits: you always try a promo code at checkout - if you saw a discount promised anywhere on the site, you expect it to work
you skim any newsletter offer for the coupon terms

buyers.name: Gemma Whitfield
buyers.backstory: Primary school teacher in Leeds who read a blog post about circular pattern drawing and wants in.
buyers.errand: Buy the Zendala / pattern-drawing course. You are in the UK and get annoyed when prices are only in dollars.
traits: international buyer wary of shipping and currency
bail_triggers: price currency is ambiguous at the moment of paying
no refund policy findable before paying
buyers.trust_needs: knowing exactly what you'll be charged in pounds, and what happens if the course isn't for you
habits: you look for a refund/returns line in the footer before you pay
you glance at the blog to confirm the seller knows their craft

buyers.name: Priya Raghunathan
buyers.backstory: Life coach with a small practice; has budgeted serious money this quarter for one certification that adds a creative tool to her sessions.
buyers.errand: Enroll today in the coaching certification. Compare the payment options carefully - full price vs split - and pick the cheaper total.
bail_triggers: a buy button that doesn't work
not being able to tell what the total cost actually is
buyers.trust_needs: clear tiers, working buttons, and certainty about what currency you're paying in
habits: you click every pricing option to compare before choosing
you scan the nav to understand what this school actually offers

buyers.name: Dawn Kowalczyk
buyers.backstory: Recently retired office manager who wants a weekly creative appointment with other adults.
buyers.errand: Join the weekly-drawing membership today. Decide between monthly and annual - you'd pay annual if the math clearly favors it.
bail_triggers: pricing you can't do the math on
any step where you're not sure what you just agreed to
buyers.trust_needs: simple pricing you can explain to your husband afterwards
habits: you re-read a price twice before tapping buy
you look for what day/time the live sessions actually happen

buyers.name: Tom Beaulieu
buyers.backstory: Buys one self-development book a month; a podcast mentioned a new drawing-based manifesting book.
buyers.errand: Buy the book from this site. If the site sells other beginner things, maybe add one - but the book is the mission.
bail_triggers: being bounced around more than 4 pages without finding the book
buyers.trust_needs: a direct path to the thing you came for
habits: you try the store/shop section first for any product
you look for a search box when you can't find something

buyers.name: Aisha Nakamura-Bell
buyers.backstory: Startup PM between meetings; a friend said 'take the basics course, it's the right entry point'.
buyers.errand: Find and buy the beginner/basics NeuroGraphica course in under 8 steps. You have five minutes.
bail_triggers: any dead end or error page
any step that makes you re-navigate from scratch
buyers.trust_needs: the path just working on the first try
habits: you take the most prominent matching button on the homepage and go

buyers.name: Colin McTavish
buyers.backstory: Semi-retired accountant whose GP suggested a mindful hobby; he has another art-course site open in a second tab and will pick one this week.
buyers.errand: Decide whether this school beats the other tab. Verify: who teaches it, what it costs, what past students say, and what happens if you want your money back.
traits: comparison shopper with a competitor mentally open in another tab
bail_triggers: claims with nothing to back them
no findable refund terms
buyers.trust_needs: verifiable humans, prices without surprises, policies in writing
habits: you read testimonials and judge whether they smell real or planted
you check the graduates/alumni page as proof the school delivers
you open the About page to see who you'd be paying

buyers.name: Renata Sowińska
buyers.backstory: Yoga instructor curious about adding drawing to her classes; burned once by a course that was a webinar funnel.
buyers.errand: Work out who actually teaches each course here and whether they're credible. You care about the person more than the price.
bail_triggers: hype language with no faces or names behind it
buyers.trust_needs: real teacher identities, live social accounts that match the site
habits: you tap the social icons to see if the accounts are active and match the site
you check the About page before any course page

buyers.name: Dr. Lena Fairweather
buyers.backstory: Art therapist assessing whether the teacher-training here is worth recommending to her supervision group.
buyers.errand: Find out how to become certified to teach this method: requirements, dates, cost, and whether enrollment is even open right now.
bail_triggers: dates that have already passed presented as upcoming
no way to get the answer without handing over your email
buyers.trust_needs: current, dated, concrete program information
habits: you cross-check the certification page against any 'upcoming programmes' page for consistency

buyers.name: Harold Njoroge
buyers.backstory: 62-year-old with low vision who browses with text zoomed to 200%; wants one affordable course to start.
buyers.errand: Compare the two cheaper drawing courses and work out how they differ - they look similar and cost the same. Pick one.
traits: low-vision buyer who bumps browser zoom to 200% when text is small
bail_triggers: text you can't read even zoomed
being unable to tell two products apart
buyers.trust_needs: legible differences between offerings
habits: you zoom into product imagery and price text
you check the beginner/basics option first if one exists

buyers.name: Sofía Andrade
buyers.backstory: Graphic designer scrolling in bed at 11:40pm; followed a reel about 'drawing your feelings'.
buyers.errand: Wander. See what this place is, save anything interesting for tomorrow-you. You are not buying tonight.
bail_triggers: anything that interrupts the scroll (popup, forced signup)
buyers.trust_needs: a vibe worth coming back to in daylight
habits: you graze the homepage end to end
you open the blog if a headline catches you
you never give your email on a first visit

buyers.name: Bernard Osei-Tutu
buyers.backstory: Recently widowed retiree; his daughter said 'look at this art site, Dad'. Uses the computer carefully, one click at a time.
buyers.errand: Look around the courses and understand what's on offer and roughly what things cost. Report back to your daughter.
bail_triggers: getting lost with no obvious way back (you click the logo to reset)
buyers.trust_needs: prices visible where the products are listed
habits: you open the catalog and expect prices on the shelf, like a shop window
you click the logo when confused

buyers.name: Keisha Lamarre
buyers.backstory: 20-something barista who arrived from a TikTok about pattern drawing; will give this site 90 seconds of thumb time.
buyers.errand: Skim the homepage; tap at most two things that catch your eye. Decide if this is 'for you' or 'for someone's aunt'.
bail_triggers: a popup before you've seen a single product
walls of text
buyers.trust_needs: instant visual proof this is your kind of thing
habits: you judge hard on the first screen
you tap a social icon if the site feels thin

buyers.name: Linda Pemberton-Ruiz
buyers.backstory: Buying a birthday present for her mother-in-law, who fills adult coloring books and 'doesn't need more objects'.
buyers.errand: Buy a drawing course as a GIFT, budget $60. Critically: figure out how it would reach her mother-in-law and not you.
bail_triggers: no way to tell if a purchase can be gifted
checkout clearly tying the course to YOUR email with no alternative
buyers.trust_needs: explicit gift wording, or at least a hint the access email can differ from the payer
habits: you hunt for a 'gift' option everywhere before giving up
you try a promo code if the site offered one

buyers.name: Margaret Ashcroft-Boyle
buyers.backstory: Solicitor in Bristol; her best friend is off work with burnout and loved a pattern-art workshop once. Budget £80.
buyers.errand: Choose between gifting the membership or the pattern-drawing course, in POUNDS, under £80. Decide and get to the point of payment.
bail_triggers: not being able to tell whether you'd be charged in £ or $
buyers.trust_needs: pound pricing that stays consistent from page to checkout
habits: you look for a currency selector
you compare the two candidate gifts on total cost and 'giftability'

buyers.name: Devon Marsh
buyers.backstory: Sends his sister a book every Christmas; this year she asked for 'that manifesting drawing book'.
buyers.errand: Get the book as a gift from this site. If the site can't sell it to you directly, note where it sends you and how that feels.
bail_triggers: being sent somewhere unexpected without warning
buyers.trust_needs: clarity about who is actually selling you the thing
habits: you check a store section first, then anywhere 'book' is mentioned

buyers.name: Yuki Tanabe-Ferris
buyers.backstory: Bought the chakra drawing course two months ago on her laptop; now on her phone in a waiting room, wants lesson 3.
buyers.errand: Get to YOUR course content. You know you have an account; you don't remember if this phone is logged in (it isn't).
bail_triggers: not being able to find where members go
a login that offers no way to recover access
buyers.trust_needs: an obvious members' door and a working way back into your account
habits: you look for 'library' or 'my courses' in the menu
you check what the login page offers if your password is forgotten (don't actually submit a reset)

buyers.name: Franklin Adeyemi
buyers.backstory: Member for four months; joined for the Thursday live sessions and wants to confirm this week's time and topic.
buyers.errand: Find out when/what this Thursday's live members' session is, without asking anyone. You're already sold; this is about logistics.
bail_triggers: schedule information existing only behind email
buyers.trust_needs: the site telling members things without a login wall for basics
habits: you check the membership page for schedule details
you try the library/members area

buyers.name: Carmen Villanueva-Reyes
buyers.backstory: Attended a drawing workshop on holiday; the facilitator said 'I'm certified - look me up on the official directory'.
buyers.errand: Find that facilitator directory and look for anyone based in Spain, or at least confirm your workshop leader is listed (any Spanish-sounding name will do as a proxy).
bail_triggers: a directory you can't search or narrow
buyers.trust_needs: a directory that works like a directory
habits: you try to search or filter before scrolling a long list
you use the site search if one exists

buyers.name: Roger Hutchins
buyers.backstory: Wants to ask one pre-sales question ('do the live sessions work from Australia's timezone?') before spending anything.
buyers.errand: Find a way to contact the school - form, email, chat, anything - and note what the site offers when you have a question money depends on.
bail_triggers: no human-reachable channel at all
buyers.trust_needs: a store that can be reached before it takes your money
habits: you check the footer first for contact links, then policies, then any FAQ
you look for a chat bubble
